title: NASA Michoud Assembly Facility 60th Anniversary
description: For more than 60 years NASA’s Michoud Assembly Facility in New Orleans has manufactured all NASA vehicles for human space flight, including the NASA's Space Launch System used for the NASA Artemis missions to the Moon and beyond. With the launch of Artemis I on the near horizon, Michoud celebrates all employees who over the last six decades worked tirelessly to help advance NASA's mission of space exploration. The un-crewed Artemis I mission is the inaugural launch of the SLS and NASA’s Orion Spacecraft as an integrated system.

transcript.text: New Orleans, a city like no other. A city
known for its culture, food, Sportsmen’s
paradise, and entertainment.
A city born over 300 years ago and
like the mighty Mississippi, good times
are still flowing.
Our hearts and souls are embedded into the
history of New Orleans. So too is the
NASA Michoud Assembly Facility.
Since 1961, Michoud has manufactured
rockets, external tanks, and hardware for
all human space flights.
The heartbeats of those who’ve worked
throughout the Apollo, Space Shuttle, and
and now the Artemis program are ones
filled with pride, dedication and ring
louder than a bass drum in a New Orleans
jazz band.
For more than 60 years, the Michoud
Assembly Facility has been known as
“America’s Rocket Factory,” manufacturing
rockets for all 13 Apollo missions and
135 external tanks for the Space Shuttle
program.
And today, we’re proud to continue NASA’s
mission, which will take the first woman
and the first person of color to the Moon
with production of the core stage rockets
and Orion spacecraft.
Everyday at Michoud, we are making
history.  It’s right here in New Orleans,
where NASA, and its partners Boeing and
Lockheed Martin are constructing the core
stage and the Orion spacecraft.
Towering at 212 feet tall, the core stage
is the biggest component of the SLS rocket
Built by Michoud employees, the core stage
consists of state-of-the-art manufacturing
and is crafted using friction-stir-welding
tooling that is the largest of its kind in
the world. NASA’s SLS rocket is the only
rocket powerful enough to send the Orion
spacecraft, astronauts, and supplies on
bold exploration missions to the Moon and
beyond.
Also manufactured at Michoud, the Orion
crew module will take us farther than
we’ve ever gone before.  Through advanced
manufacturing and technology, the Orion
pressure vessel with the launch abort
system can activate within milliseconds to
propel the vehicle to safety in case of an
emergency. For the first time in a
generation, NASA has built a human
spacecraft for deep-space missions that
will usher in a new era of
space exploration.
With an astonishing 43 acres of
manufacturing and assembly space under one
roof, engineers, technicians, and students
in aerospace engineering can design, build
and outfit the SLS core stages and Orion
spacecraft with avionics, thermal
protection systems, and other critical
internal hardware to create the
perfect vehicle fit for a goddess… Artemis
For the last six decades, all NASA
vehicles for human space flight have gone
and continue to go through New Orleans.
The spirit of Michoud is the pride
and dedication of our people.
As you can see, the path to the Moon and
Mars begins in the Crescent City. Are you
new journey?
